item.title: Computer-assisted proofs of periodic solutions of state-dependent delay equations beyond perturbative regimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.36216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rigorous existence results for periodic solutions of state-dependent delay differential equations (SDDEs) are scarce outside perturbative regimes, where the equation is close to an ordinary or constant-delay differential equation. We develop a computer-assisted framework that proves the existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs directly. The numerical approximation is a trigonometric polynomial, and a true periodic solution nearby is obtained by a Newton--Kantorovich argument in the space of $C^1$ periodic functions. The main difficulty lies in the terms in which the solution is evaluated at a time that itself depends on the solution. We obtain rigorous enclosures of their Fourier coefficients by adapting validated discrete Fourier transform techniques for analytic nonlinearities. We apply the framework to three representative examples of increasing complexity: a periodically forced toy model, an autonomous scalar equation with two state-dependent delays, and a threshold-type delay model from operon dynamics in gene regulation. To our knowledge, these are the first computer-assisted proofs of existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs outside perturbative regimes. This opens the way to computer-assisted proofs for SDDEs more broadly. All computer-assisted proofs, including the requisite codes and the approximate objects, are accessible on GitHub at \cite{code_proof}.
item.dc:creator: Jan Bouwe van den Berg, Maxime Breden, Matthieu Cadiot, Kevin E. M. Church, Jean-Philippe Lessard

item.title: Boundary and Interior of Root Sets of Power Series
item.description: arXiv:2610.36279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the set $\mathcal{M}_M$ of roots of power series with coefficients in $\{0, \pm 1, ..., \pm M \}$ and constant coefficient $1$. We prove that every nonreal root in the unit disk of a polynomial of this form is an interior point of $\mathcal{M}_M$. Moreover we establish a dimension formula and show the corresponding Hausdorff measure is finite and positive for a family of attractors parameterized by boundary parameters $\lambda \in \partial \mathcal{M}_M \setminus \mathbb{R}$. Finally we show that $\partial \mathcal{M}_M$ has Lebesgue measure zero.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Kewarth

item.title: Complete Expanding Interval Maps are Mixing
item.description: arXiv:2610.36292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a new and elementary\footnote{That is: without functional analysis.} proof that certain smooth, complete, expanding maps from the interval to itself are mixing.
item.dc:creator: E. L. O'Neil, F. M. Tangerman, J. J. P. Veerman

item.title: Integer points for iterated Weierstrass elliptic functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.36323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Iterated Weierstrass P functions exhibit relationships between period lattices and the dynamics. We connect the dynamical properties to the occurrence of integer and rational points on associated real elliptic curves. Defining a complex number z to be an integer point if both P(z) and P'(z) are integers, we restrict to P when the lattice is real and its invariants g2 and g3 are integers. We study when an integer point lies in the Fatou set of P and when it lies in the Julia set, and if there is any dynamical significance to this. Applying established results on integer solutions to cubic Diophantine equations to the dynamical properties of iterated elliptic P functions, we show integer points at poles of P lie in the Julia set. Integer points can also occur in the Fatou set of P.
item.dc:creator: Jane Hawkins

item.title: Variations of the harmonic entropy and linear drift on negatively curved surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.36354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For closed negatively curved surfaces, we obtain formulas for the derivatives of the harmonic entropy of its geodesic flow and the linear drift of its Brownian motion along conformal deformations. We deduce that the harmonic entropy of the geodesic flow of a closed surface of non-constant negative curvature (resp. linear drift of the Brownian motion on its universal cover) is strictly decreasing (resp. increasing) along the normalized Ricci flow. We also prove that any hyperbolic metric on a surface admits a neighborhood in the space of conformal negatively curved metrics in which the linear drift is greater or equal to the Liouville entropy, with equality if and only if the metric is hyperbolic.
item.dc:creator: Karen Butt, Alena Erchenko, Tristan Humbert

item.title: Quasi-periodic tree sets and structure trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.36451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We expand our discussion of the almost stability theorem of Dicks and Dunwoody in the context of probability measure preserving equivalence relations.
item.dc:creator: Mikael Pichot

item.title: A Homological Approach to Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.36532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note describes a novel approach to systematically characterize dynamics based on finite information. We present an algebraic framework for dynamics from which it is possible to deduce more traditional descriptors associated with the qualitative structures of the geometric theory of dynamical systems. The purpose of this paper is to indicate how this approach can be used to obtain interpretable characterizations of dynamics that are robust with respect to perturbations, in the context of models of multiscale and data-driven systems.
item.dc:creator: William Kalies, Konstantin Mischaikow, Robert Vandervorst

item.title: Periodic Solutions and Exponential Attractivity in Hopfield-Type Neural Networks with Generalized Piecewise Constant Arguments: Impulsive and Nonimpulsive Cases
item.description: arXiv:2610.36560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate an impulsive Hopfield-type neural network with a generalized piecewise constant argument, including the nonimpulsive case in which all jump terms vanish. The piecewise constant argument is given by $\gamma(t)=\zeta_k$ on each interval $[t_k,t_{k+1})$, where $t_k\leq\zeta_k\leq t_{k+1}$, $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$. Depending on the position of $\zeta_k$, the argument may be advanced, retarded, or of mixed type. By representing periodic solutions through a Green function and applying a fixed-point argument, we obtain explicit and verifiable sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an $\omega$-periodic solution. We then use a Gronwall-type estimate, together with period averages, to prove that this solution is globally exponentially attractive. These conditions can be checked directly from the system parameters, without requiring explicit knowledge of the periodic solution. In the course of the analysis, we also revisit and correct some estimates presented by Pinto et al. \cite{Pinto_ejqtde}. The case $\zeta_k=t_k$ reduces to their setting, whereas our results cover the more general choice of $\zeta_k$ within each interval. We also present examples illustrating different types of piecewise constant arguments.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Torres Naranjo, Samuel Castillo Apolonio

item.title: Geometric structures, orbit closures and invariant measures in moduli spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.36893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on the seminal work of Eskin, Mirzakhani and Mohammadi in the context of dynamics on moduli spaces, we introduce linear loci and linear measures to provide a relatively basic description of orbit closures and invariant measures in strata of translation surfaces. We use this to discuss geometrical properties of orbit closures and invariant measures from the perspective of geometric structures.
item.dc:creator: John Smillie, Florent Ygouf

item.title: Fractal transference principle for conformal iterated function systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.37119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a complex one-dimensional fractal transference principle connecting density combinatorics with the fractal geometry of complex continued fractions. Our framework applies to a broad class of conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points, including those associated with the Hurwitz continued fraction, and transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to digit sets while preserving the maximal Hausdorff dimension. As applications, we obtain fractal counterparts of the multidimensional and polynomial Szemer\'edi theorems, as well as their relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green--Tao theorem.
item.dc:creator: Yuto Nakajima, Hiroki Takahasi

item.title: Non-convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics: The bounded influence model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a recent preprint, we found counterexamples to a number of auxiliary conjectures in a 2012 paper of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo, concerning convergence in two fundamental models of heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics, the synchronized bounded confidence (SBC) and synchronized bounded influence (SBI) models. Building on our work, Etesami and Touri presented an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBC dynamics, resolving the main conjecture from the 2012 paper in that case. Here we complete this project by presenting an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBI dynamics. The example was found with the help of AI.
item.dc:creator: Peter Hegarty, Damiano Ognissanti, Edvin Wedin

item.title: The K-property of equilibrium states for systems with non-uniform structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.37392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a general criterion for the K-property of equilibrium states within the Climenhaga-Thompson framework. Under suitable pressure-gap and non-uniform expansiveness assumptions, we show that the unique equilibrium state has the K-property, provided that the good collection of orbit segments satisfies an appropriate non-uniform specification property, as well as an appropriate non-uniform distortion control property for the potential function. These results do not require any additional lambda-decomposition structure and apply to a wide range of systems, including those with non-trivial central directions, such as the frame flow over closed rank-one manifolds with bunched nonpositive curvature. Moreover, we also construct several counterexamples to demonstrate that generally the assumptions in our criteria cannot be weakened while keeping the K-property.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Wang

item.title: Measure of Maximal Entropy for Geodesic Flows on Noncompact Manifolds of Nonpositive Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.37439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the variational characterization of the measure of maximal entropy on noncompact manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature. Assuming that the deck transformation group contains an axial isometry with a rank-one axis and has a finite critical exponent, we prove that the supremum of the entropies of invariant probabilities equals the critical exponent and is attained if and only if the Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) measure is finite. In that case, the measure of maximal entropy is unique and equals the normalized BMS measure. The proof combines conditional-entropy rigidity on the regular set with an HTS-based entropy exclusion on the singular set, overcoming both non-compactness and the loss of uniform hyperbolicity due to zero curvature. We also obtain mixing under a non-arithmetic length-spectrum assumption. For nonpositively curved surfaces of genus at least two, the existence of a closed Jacobi rank-one geodesic and the non-arithmeticity of the axial length spectrum are automatic.
item.dc:creator: Fei Liu, Xiaokai Liu

item.title: Multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds and the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.37468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish uniform multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds for polynomials of Zakeri type, where all free critical points are on the boundary of an invariant Siegel disk of bounded type. This generalizes the unicritical result~\cite{DL:wZ}. As an application, we show the optimality of the Brjuno condition under the Zakeri restriction: as the rotation number becomes non-Brjuno, the Siegel disk evolves into the Cremer Hedgehog. Combined with~\cite{BCR26}, this implies the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials, resolving a conjecture by Douady from the 1980s.
item.dc:creator: Dzmitry Dudko, Yusheng Luo, Runze Zhang

item.title: The Assouad Dimension of Graphs: An Affirmative Answer to Fraser's Question
item.description: arXiv:2610.37477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article primarily investigates the Assouad dimension of graphs of continuous functions. Initially, the Assouad spectrum of the graph of a H\"older and count-H\"older continuous function has been derived. It has been shown that the Assouad dimension of the graph of a continuous function $f:[a,b]\to \mathbb{R}$ with the count-H\"older condition is at least \( 1 + \sup \left\{ \overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}L_f(y) : y \in \mathscr{R}_f[a,b]\right\} \) where $\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}$ denotes the upper box dimension, $L_f(y)$ is the level set of $f$ at level $y$, and $\mathscr{R}_f[a,b]$ is the range of $f$ on $[a,b]$. As a consequence, non-trivial lower bounds are obtained for the Assouad dimension of the graphs of classical functions such as the Weierstrass and Takagi functions. We have also employed a unified projection solely in the direction of the $y$-axis to establish lower and upper bounds for the Assouad dimension. On this basis, we have shown that the lower bound is sharp in terms of level sets, namely the upper box dimension cannot be replaced by the Assouad dimension. This provides a partial positive answer to Question 17.11.1 posed by Fraser in~\cite{Fraser2021}, and to Question 2.2 posed by Yu in~\cite{Yu2020}. Building on this result, the analysis has been further extended to a broader class of Weierstrass-type functions and some self-affine functions like fractal interpolation functions. Moreover, we have discussed certain circumstances under which the Assouad dimension can reach 2 with several examples constructed. A supplementary explanation of why Brownian motion has the full Assouad dimension has also been provided based on the preceding work of Howroyd and Yu \cite{Howroyd2019}.
item.dc:creator: Binyan Yu, Bilel Selmi, Jia Liu, Yongshun Liang

item.title: Minimal acceleration and the topology of premonotonic cocycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In his global theory of one-frequency Schr\"odinger operators~\cite{Av15}, Avila asked whether the acceleration of a real-analytic $\SL(2,\R)$ cocycle over an irrational circle rotation is bounded below by the absolute value of its topological degree and whether equality in nonzero degree characterizes premonotonicity. We answer this question affirmatively for every irrational frequency, without arithmetic restrictions. Here premonotonicity means that some iterate becomes strictly monotonic in the base variable after a periodic change of coordinates~\cite{AK15}. In the positive Lyapunov exponent regime, this provides a nonzero-degree counterpart to Avila's characterization of uniform hyperbolicity by vanishing acceleration. In nonzero degree, we also characterize minimal acceleration through signed connections and invariant positive matrix-valued measures. In the positive-degree, positive Lyapunov exponent case, the proof constructs an analytic positive connection using invariant positive matrix-valued measures and a transfer--scattering representation. A complex-analytic construction then produces a periodic gauge. As a further consequence, for each fixed irrational frequency and nonzero degree, the premonotonic locus is path connected: every cocycle in this locus can be joined to the linear rotation of the same degree by a path preserving premonotonicity.
item.dc:creator: Xu Xia, Jiahao Xu

item.title: Polynomial automorphisms of C^2 with the same equilibrium measure
item.description: arXiv:2610.37600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We review the following question: when do two polynomial automorphisms of C^2 have the same maximal entropy measure? While the answer has been known for some time when both automorphisms are compositions of H\'enon maps, the general case is more delicate. In this (mostly expository) note we explain how recent results in random dynamics give an almost complete solution to the question, and point out a number of related open problems.
item.dc:creator: Romain Dujardin

item.title: Contact topology and intrinsic characterization of transversely vanishing curl eigenforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.36212v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the geometry and topology of transversely vanishing eigenforms of the curl operator on $3$-manifolds, placing them in the broader framework of near-contact forms. We prove a Gray-type stability theorem for the kernels of near-contact forms, which we call near-contact structures, and derive a local neighborhood theorem around their singularities. As applications, we obtain a stability result for the contact topology of curl eigenforms, a classification of near-contact structures in terms of formal homotopical data, and a proof of the existence of contact structures on closed orientable 3-manifolds based on the spectral theory of the curl operator. We also study the symplectization of curl eigenforms as a possible bridge to symplectic dynamics. Finally, we characterize those transversely vanishing $1$-forms which are curl eigenforms for some smooth Riemannian metric. We deduce a generalization of the classical correspondence, due to Etnyre and Ghrist, between Reeb-like fields of contact forms and nowhere-vanishing rotational Beltrami fields to the setting of transversely vanishing vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Robert Cardona, Willi Kepplinger

item.title: Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control via Trajectory Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.36342v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The curse of dimensionality associated with solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for the value function remains a key obstacle for real-time optimal feedback control of high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems. This is especially severe in aerospace applications such as relaminarizing unsteady turbulent flows and recovering from aerodynamic stall where nonlinear dynamics play a significant role. We introduce Balanced Active Subspaces for Optimal Control (BASOC), a model reduction framework which seeks to find directions in state space along which the value function is most sensitive, and the distribution of states exhibits maximum variance along optimal trajectories. BASOC leverages trajectory optimization and the Pontryagin minimum principle to obtain state and co-state (value function gradient) data along locally optimal trajectories for constructing state and gradient covariance matrices. Balancing these matrices provides an oblique projection for approximating the value function, which can also be used to construct reduced-order models and surrogate feedback control laws. We show that for linear-quadratic optimal control problems, BASOC becomes equivalent to a snapshot method for initial condition balancing of the optimally controlled closed-loop realization. The framework is demonstrated on a nonlinear three-dimensional system where POD and balanced truncation are known to perform poorly, and on the nonlinear complex Ginzburg-Landau equation to demonstrate feasibility for larger-scale systems.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel S. Ameh, Samuel E. Otto

item.title: Exact Generic Exponents of Approximation for the Action of the Integral Special Linear Group on the Torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.36397v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given an integer $n\ge 2$ and points $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ lying in the $n$--dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^n$ equipped with its usual metric denoted by $\left\langle\;\cdot\;\right\rangle$, let \[ \tau_n(\mathbf x,\mathbf y) = \sup\left\{ \tau\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{there exist infinitely many } H\ge1\text{ for which}\\[1mm] \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-\tau} \text{ for some } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z) \end{array} \right\} \] be the Diophantine exponent of asymptotic approximation of $\mathbf{y}$ by the orbit of $\mathbf{x}$ under the action of the integral special linear group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$. Let also \[ \widehat{\tau}_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right) = \sup\left\{ \tau\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{for all but finitely many } H\ge1, \text{ there is } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\\[1mm] \text{such that } \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-\tau} \end{array} \right\} \] denote the corresponding exponent of uniform approximation. The main result of this paper proves that for almost all $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{T}^n$ (with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure), $$\widehat{\tau}_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; \tau_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; n-1.$$ This is the first result to establish the exact generic approximation exponents for an action of a lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$ induced by the standard Euclidean action.
item.dc:creator: Faustin Adiceam, R\'egis Aolo

item.title: Almost Periodicity Properties Arising From the Sodin-Yuditskii Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.36403v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Kotani-Last problem and the Deift conjecture are two well known statements, which both concern the almost periodicity properties of the functions under consideration, and which have both been disproved in their original formulation, which involves Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity. To contrast these disproofs, and to further elucidate the essence of these two challenging problems, we establish positive results regarding each of them by showing that Weyl almost periodicity can be deduced whenever the Sodin-Yuditskii setup can be implemented. The latter requires that the Schr\"odinger operator associated with the function in question has purely absolutely continuous spectral measure and a spectrum with finite total gap length and the Parreau-Widom property. We also show that the known examples for which Bohr/Bochner almost periodicity has been shown or suggested to fail in the context of the Deift conjecture are in fact Weyl almost periodic. As a result, an accordingly modified version of the Deift conjecture remains a tantalizing open problem.
item.dc:creator: David Damanik (Rice University), Long Li (Texas A&M University), Nicolae Strungaru (MacEwan University)

item.title: Large deviations from a stable steady state for damped dispersive PDEs with vanishing random kicks
item.description: arXiv:2610.36815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the behaviour of stationary measures for a class of dispersive PDEs damped by a linear zero-order term and perturbed by a small kick noise. Under some natural assumptions on the law of the noise, we prove that any family of stationary measures satisfies the large deviation principle in the vanishing noise limit. The result highlights the role of nonlinear smoothing and applies to the nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Korteweg-de Vries equations, and to a variety of random perturbations including Gaussian and exponential variables.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Chen, Armen Shirikyan, Shengquan Xiang

item.title: Exploring Neural Dynamics with Time Delays: A Numerical and Bifurcation Analysis Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.36920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Wilson-Cowan model is a classic example of a ``neural mass model'' - a simplified yet powerful way to describe the activity of large networks of neurons. It is particularly interesting because, even in its relatively simple form, it can produce a surprising variety of behaviours, from steady rhythms to complex oscillations. A key factor influencing these dynamics is the presence of time delays, reflecting the time it takes for signals to travel between neurons. This article offers an accessible introduction to the Wilson-Cowan model, focusing on how these time delays affect its behaviour. We explore the core concepts behind the model, survey the existing literature, and introduce some numerical techniques specifically designed for analysing such delay differential equations. We also provide a practical, hands-on tutorial on using the DDE-BIFTOOL software package, demonstrating its application to the Wilson-Cowan model. Downloadable code allows the reader to reproduce our results and to explore the model's dynamics further, including MATLAB code for all computations, using DDE-BIFTOOL for the continuation, and Python versions of simulation codes.
item.dc:creator: Martin R Nelson, Jonathan J Crofts

item.title: Stationary Coexistence in Stochastic Gause Systems with General Trophic Responses
item.description: arXiv:2610.37372v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study stationary coexistence in stochastic Gause predator-prey systems with independent multiplicative environmental noise and trophic responses depending on both population densities. A weighted population balance cancels the trophic interaction and yields moments of order greater than one without imposing predator self-regulation. These estimates give a direct occupation-measure proof of a sufficient coexistence criterion based on prey establishment and predator invasion of the prey-only stationary environment. For responses whose rare-predator limit is strictly increasing and whose value at positive predator density never exceeds that limit, we also establish necessity of positive predator invasion whenever the prey-only stationary law exists. If the prey per-capita growth attains its global maximum at zero, interior stationarity itself forces prey establishment, giving a necessary-and-sufficient criterion beyond logistic growth. Logistic and bounded saturating growth laws provide explicit Gamma and beta-prime resident distributions. Applications include Holling, Ivlev, Beddington-DeAngelis, and Crowley-Martin responses. Responses with the same rare-predator limit share the coexistence threshold, although predator interference changes the interior distribution. Reproducible quadrature and simulations illustrate this distinction. The analysis builds on existing stochastic persistence theory and identifies precisely the additional comparison argument needed for necessity, including exclusion of interior invariant measures at zero predator invasion.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'es S\'anchez, Leon A. Valencia, Jorge M. Ramirez Osorio

item.title: A semigroup approach for rough partial differential equations with jumps
item.description: arXiv:2610.37401v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish an infinite-dimensional sewing lemma for discontinuous paths on a scale of Banach spaces. This allows us to construct Young and rough convolutions with jumps. Based on this we analyze the local and global well-posedness of semilinear parabolic rough partial differential equations (PDEs) with jumps in mixed space-time regularity spaces.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Blessing Neam\c{t}u, Hongjun Gao, Haoyuan Li

item.title: Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.37573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface. We give a lower bound for the $L^2$ norm of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact part of the surface. This extends a result of Soundararajan [arXiv:0901.4060] to the nonarithmetic setting. The crucial components of the proof are a long-time Egorov's theorem designed for this setting, a nonlinear uncertainty principle of Cohen--Dyatlov [arXiv:2609.30261], and an application of Weyl's method for exponential sums.
item.dc:creator: Alex Cohen, Zhenhao Li, Zhongkai Tao

item.title: A Product on Lorenz Hulls, Zonoids, and Vector Measure Ranges
item.description: arXiv:2309.09790v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Lorenz skeleton and Lorenz hull are the range and the convex hull of the range of an $\mathbb{R}^n$-valued measure, respectively. A Lorenz hull is also known as a zonoid. We extend the tensor product of centered zonoids introduced by Aubrun and Lancien and developed by Breiding et al. to Lorenz hulls without a centering restriction, and further to Lorenz skeletons. We show that this product admits a direct interpretation in terms of the elementary notion of a product measure. Inclusion preservation and Hausdorff continuity, shown by Aubrun and Lancien and Breiding et al., respectively, for centered zonoids, hold in this more general setting as well.
item.dc:creator: John Steinberger, Zhe Zhang

item.title: Infinite unrestricted sumsets in subsets of abelian groups with large density
item.description: arXiv:2504.08649v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(G,+)$ be a countable abelian group such that the subgroup $\{g+g\colon g\in G\}$ has finite index and the doubling map $g\mapsto g+g$ has finite kernel. We establish lower bounds on the upper density of a set $A\subset G$ with respect to an appropriate F{\o}lner sequence, so that $A$ contains a sumset of the form $\{t+b_1+b_2\colon b_1,b_2\in B\}$ or $\{b_1+b_2\colon b_1,b_2\in B\}$, for some infinite $B\subset G$ and some $t\in G$. Both assumptions on $G$ are necessary for our results to be true. We also characterize the F{\o}lner sequences for which this is possible. Finally, we show that our lower bounds are optimal in a strong sense.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Charamaras, Ioannis Kousek, Andreas Mountakis, Trist\'an Radi\'c

item.title: Counting Saddle Connections on Hyperelliptic Translation Surfaces with a Slit
item.description: arXiv:2601.15993v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider saddle connections on a translation surface in a hyperelliptic connected component of a stratum that do not intersect the interior of a distinguished saddle connection. For this restricted set of saddle connections, we show that it satisfies an $L (\log L)^{d-2}$ growth rate, where $d$ is the complex dimension of the hyperelliptic stratum. The upper bound holds for all translation surfaces in the hyperelliptic stratum while the lower bound holds for almost every surface in the hyperelliptic stratum. The proof of the lower bound uses horocycle renormalization.
item.dc:creator: David Aulicino, Howard Masur, Huiping Pan, Weixu Su

item.title: Solvable Lie Foliations on Compact Five-Manifolds: Classification, Cohomological Obstruction, and Non-Homogeneous Examples
item.description: arXiv:2604.04965v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study $\GA$-Lie foliations on compact five-manifolds. We establish a structural classification of the holonomy group $\Gamma$ into five types according to its algebraic structure inside $\GA$. For three of these types (I, II, IIIa) we prove homogeneity via Meigniez's theorem and the Matsumoto--Tsuchiya theorem. For Type~IIIb we prove non-homogeneity by exhibiting a non-polycyclic holonomy group, extending the Dathe--Ndiaye construction \cite{DN11}. We introduce a cohomological class $[F]\in H^2(\Gamma^{\mathrm{ab}},[\Gamma,\Gamma])$ as a \emph{necessary} obstruction to homogeneity: if $\mathcal{F}$ is homogeneous and $\Gamma$ is polycyclic then $[F]=0$. We show that Type IIIb foliations satisfy $[F]\neq 0$. For Type IIIc, we prove that certain foliations are non-homogeneous by a direct argument when the generating translations are $\Q(\lambda)$-linearly independent; we exhibit explicit homogeneous examples showing that this type is \emph{not} universally non-homogeneous. Finally, we construct the first known non-homogeneous $\mathrm{Sol}$-Lie foliation in dimension five by a verified lattice deformation.
item.dc:creator: Ameth Ndiaye

item.title: Locally invariant manifolds and foliations
item.description: arXiv:2604.18202v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Invariant manifolds and foliations associated to invariant pseudo-hyperbolic reference geometries have been well-studied in the context of dynamics implemented by a diffeomorphism. In this paper, we provide sufficient conditions for the existence of maximally smooth, \emph{locally} invariant manifolds and foliations containing a given \emph{locally} invariant, pseudo-hyperbolic reference geometry, in the context of dynamics implemented by a smooth map which need not be invertible. The theory is motivated by applications to the developing theory of large-step optimisation.
item.dc:creator: Lachlan Ewen MacDonald

item.title: Continuum-wise hyperbolicity is exactly the pseudo-Anosov dynamics with spine singularities
item.description: arXiv:2606.11943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a complete structural classification for cw$_F$-hyperbolic surface homeomorphisms. Specifically, we prove that a surface homeomorphism is cw$_F$-hyperbolic if, and only if, it is a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism whose singularities consist exclusively of spines (1-prongs). Furthermore, we classify these systems up to topological conjugacy, showing that every such homeomorphism is conjugate to either an Anosov automorphism on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or to a standard hyperelliptic quotient on $\mathbb{S}^2$ of a hyperbolic affine toral map. As a rigid consequence of this classification, we show that such dynamics are strictly obstructed on surfaces of genus greater than one, the Klein bottle, and the projective plane.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Arruda, Bernardo Carvalho, Piotr Oprocha, Alberto Sarmiento

item.title: Compactifications of Abelian Group Bundles and a Topological Halmos--von Neumann-type Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2608.28335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The topological Halmos--von Neumann theorem is a fundamental result of topological dynamics that completely classifies continuous actions of abelian topological groups which are ergodic and have discrete spectrum. It rests on a correspondence between such actions (up to the choice of a distinguished point), compactifications of the acting group and subgroups of its dual group. We generalize both the classical statement and the underlying categorical equivalences to the framework of open group bundles over locally compact base spaces. As a byproduct, we establish a Pontryagin-type duality between \'etale Hausdorff abelian group bundles and open proper Hausdorff abelian group bundles, extending the classical duality between discrete and compact abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Anglewitz, Patrick Hermle, Henrik Kreidler

item.title: Hyperbolic area of Fatou components and new proofs of no-wandering-domain theorems
item.description: arXiv:2609.23834v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a new elementary proof of Sullivan's no-wandering-domain theorem for rational maps of degree at least two using hyperbolic area. We then develop this method further to prove that a transcendental entire function has no wandering Fatou components if its set of singular values is compact and all accumulation points of that set lie in the Fatou set. Neither proof uses quasiconformal techniques.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Ye

item.title: Marchal-type lemmas for the restricted $(N+1)$-body problem with their applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.22849v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The direct methods of calculus of variations have had a great success in the classical Newtonian $N$-body problem in this century. First in finding periodic solutions and more recently in the existence of parabolic, hyperbolic and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions. The foundation of many of these results is Marchal's lemma, which guarantee's fixed-end local minimizers are collision-free and hence classical solutions of the $N$-body problem. Meanwhile almost no result is available in the restricted problem through the direct methods of calculus of variations, mainly due to the lack of a Marchal-type lemma. In this paper such a lemma and its variation will be obtained for the restricted problem. We then apply them to the restricted problem to study unbounded (hyperbolic, parabolic, bi-hyperbolic and bi-parabolic) solutions, and bounded (periodic and quasi-periodic) solutions. We emphasize that the extension to the restricted case does not follow from the standard arguement for the unrestricted case.
item.dc:creator: Kuo-chang Chen, Guowei Yu

item.title: Silent Orbits and Cancellations in the Wave Trace
item.description: arXiv:2408.09238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper shows that the wave trace of a bounded and strictly convex planar domain may be arbitrarily smooth in a neighborhood of some point in the length spectrum. In other words, the Poisson relation, which asserts that the singular support of the wave trace is contained in the closure of $\pm$ the length spectrum, can almost be made into a strict inclusion. To do so, we construct large families of domains for which there exist multiple periodic billiard orbits having the same length but different Maslov indices. Using the microlocal Balian-Bloch-Zelditch parametrix for wave invariants developed in our previous paper, we solve a large system of equations for the boundary curvature jets, which leads to the required cancellations. We call such periodic orbits silent, since they are undetectable from the ostensibly audible wave trace. Such cancellations show that there are potential limitations in using the wave trace for inverse spectral problems and, more fundamentally, that the Laplace spectrum and the length spectrum are inherently different mathematical objects, at least insofar as the wave trace is concerned.
item.dc:creator: Illya Koval, Amir Vig

item.title: NN-OpInf: an operator inference approach using structure-preserving composable neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2603.08488v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose neural network operator inference (NN-OpInf): a structure-preserving, composable, and minimally restrictive operator inference framework for the non-intrusive reduced-order modeling of dynamical systems. The approach learns latent dynamics from snapshot data, enforcing local operator structure such as skew-symmetry, (semi-)positive definiteness, and gradient preservation, while also reflecting complex dynamics by supporting additive compositions of heterogeneous operators. We present practical training strategies and analyze computational costs relative to linear and quadratic polynomial OpInf (P-OpInf). Numerical experiments across several nonlinear and parametric problems demonstrate improved accuracy, stability, and robustness over P-OpInf and prior NN-ROM formulations, particularly when the dynamics are not well represented by polynomial models. These results suggest that NN-OpInf can serve as an effective drop-in replacement for P-OpInf when the dynamics to be modeled contain non-polynomial nonlinearities, offering potential gains in accuracy and out-of-distribution performance at the expense of higher training computational costs and a more difficult, non-convex learning problem.
item.dc:creator: Eric Parish, Anthony Gruber, Patrick Blonigan, Irina Tezaur

item.title: On aggregation-quantization permutability problem for discrete-time Markov chains
item.description: arXiv:2603.14269v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given random walk on a graph, the corresponding discrete-time quantum walk can be constructed using the method proposed by Szegedy. On the other hand, given a partition of the set of states of a Markov chain, one can study the corresponding aggregated process. We extend the aggregation technique to the level of quantum Markov chains. We provide conditions under which application of these two operations - Szegedy's quantization and aggregation - give the same result. These consist of the strong lumpability of the underlying Markov chain supplemented by nonlinear relations, generalizing Kolmogorov's cycle condition, that account for the coefficients of both the original and the aggregated transition matrices. In particular, we show that the conditions are satisfied in the case of the random walk on graphs equipped with equitable partitions. We present several examples, which include the classical/quantum walks on Platonic solids. We discuss also relation of discrete-time classical/quantum walks on $N$-dimensional hypercube and the Ehrenfests urn model with $N$ particles. We apply our technique for of discrete-time walks on Cayley graphs of free groups. We also compare our results with those obtained using Cantero-Moral-Velazquez uniformization of unitary matrices.
item.dc:creator: Adam Doliwa, Artur Siemaszko, Adam Zalewski

item.title: Structure-Aware Variational Learning of a Class of Generalized Diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2604.20188v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Learning the underlying potential energy of stochastic gradient systems from partial and noisy observations is a fundamental problem arising in physics, chemistry, and data-driven modeling. Classical approaches often rely on direct regression of governing equations or velocity fields, which can be sensitive to noise and external perturbations and may fail when observations are incomplete. In this work, we propose a structure-aware, energy-based learning framework for inferring unknown potential functions in generalized diffusion processes, grounded in the energetic variational approach. Starting from the energy-dissipation law associated with the Fokker-Planck equation, we construct loss functions based on the De Giorgi dissipation functional, which consistently couple the free energy and the dissipation mechanism of the system. This formulation avoids explicit enforcement of the governing partial differential equation and preserves the underlying variational structure of the dynamics. Through numerical experiments in one, two, and three dimensions, we demonstrate that the proposed energy-based loss exhibits enhanced robustness with respect to observation time, noise level, and the diversity and amount of available training data. These results highlight the effectiveness of energy-dissipation principles as a reliable foundation for learning stochastic diffusion dynamics from data.
item.dc:creator: Yubin Lu, Xiaofan Li, Chun Liu, Qi Tang, Yiwei Wang

item.title: The Global Empirical NTK: Self-Referential Bias and Dimensionality of Gradient Descent Learning
item.description: arXiv:2605.08746v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In training a neural network with gradient descent (GD), each iteration induces a linear operator that governs the first-order updates to a model's internal state variables. We call this operator the Global Empirical Neural Tangent Kernel (GeNTK). In finite-width networks, GeNTK is typically intractable to form, leading prior work to focus on restrictive settings, such as tracking only outputs or infinite-width limits. Here, we bridge this gap by studying the structure of GeNTK across many models. Formulating the model state as the solution to a global implicit constraint, we derive GeNTK as a product of two operators: K, accounting for immediate parameter-to-state interactions, and P, describing internal state-to-state dependencies. For a broad class of "weight-based models", such as RNNs and transformers, we prove a universal Kronecker-core theorem showing that K admits an exact, forward-pass-computable form given by the Gram matrix of weight-site variables. This core gives a measurable state-dependent restriction on Euclidean GD, termed "self-referential bias": current activity filters which adjoint directions can drive a first-order update. For recurrent models (GRUs and RNNs), we examine the spectrum of GeNTK and formalize notions of low-rank, biased learning in terms of reduced spatial or temporal ranks of the full operator. Practically, this explains why some RNN initializations yield better learning, while some plateau, by biasing the GeNTK and thus restricting learning to a small domain of learnable tasks. To demonstrate computational viability, we validate the main theorems in a self-attention transformer and a pretrained Pythia transformer language model with 410 million parameters. Overall, our results expose tractable local rank and mode-selective biases in the finite-width GD geometry and open the door to principled study of the GeNTK, a bridge between theory and practice.
item.dc:creator: James Hazelden, Laura Driscoll, Eli Shlizerman, Eric Shea-Brown

item.title: Theoretical and Computational Advances in Birkhoff Pseudospectral Transcription for Aerospace Optimal Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.17842v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Birkhoff pseudospectral methods replace the differentiation matrices of classical transcriptions with integration operators whose conditioning does not deteriorate with polynomial order. This paper presents theoretical and computational advancements toward their practical use in aerospace optimal control. The initial-point-anchored Birkhoff integration operator is constructed explicitly for flipped Legendre-Gauss-Radau grids and related exactly to the corresponding Lagrange differentiation matrix and, through a reflection, to the standard Radau Birkhoff operator, whose conditioning properties it inherits. Rate constraints on nonlinear functions of states and controls are enforced directly through the pseudospectral operators and, for control-rate limits, shown to be primal and dual equivalent to state augmentation. Non-affine time mappings concentrate the nodes around localized trajectory features, and composing affine scaling and equilibration transformations provides a systematic way to construct scaling strategies. The methods are implemented in the open-source MATLAB framework RAPTOR and tested across a range of challenging optimal control problems, including a dense-grid orbit-raising problem, a rate-limited landing scenario, a Space Shuttle entry problem, and a five-phase reusable-launch-vehicle mission.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Minnozzi, Marco Sagliano

item.title: Global invertibility of polynomial mappings and connectedness of preimages of large spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.33875v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that a polynomial mapping $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant is a global diffeomorphism provided the preimage of large circles are connected. In higher dimensions this result fails and we present families of counterexamples. Yet, in dimension $3$ with codimension of Jelonek set greater than one, we prove that if the preimages of large spheres are connected, then the Jelonek set of the mapping is neither homeomorphic to a line nor can have a single end at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Francisco Braun, Zbigniew Jelonek, Maria Michalska
